title: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines how we curate runbooks, assign incident ownership, and standardize on-call rotations, game-day exercises, postmortem output, and customer status templates. It establishes a lifecycle for runbooks (creation → review → retirement), a lightweight incident command ladder, and concrete communication templates for status page and customer notices.

Audience: on-call engineers, SREs, service owners, people-ops, and incident commanders.

Key definitions

- Service owner: team and primary engineer responsible for the long-term health of a service (maintenance, SLOs, runbooks).
- Incident commander (IC): temporary owner of incident coordination until handoff.
- Operator / responder: engineer executing runbooks.
- Runbook steward: person responsible for keeping runbooks accurate and up-to-date.

Runbook lifecycle and governance

1) Creation (initial authoring)
- Required fields for each runbook: title, service, primary steward, last-reviewed, related playbooks, severity tiers covered, prerequisites, immediate containment steps, and post-incident tasks.
- Add a short summary line at the top: single-sentence intended use.
- Naming convention: service-action-severity (e.g., runtime-prefix-eviction-P1).

2) Review cadence
- All runbooks must be reviewed at least once every 90 days. Ownership rotates quarterly with the service squad.
- Review checklist: verify commands, confirm contact names, run the smoke checks, and validate any TTL/threshold values.

3) Versioning and change history
- Inline header must include: steward, created_at, last_updated, changelog (bullet of top 3 changes).
- For substantive changes (commands/scripts updated, thresholds changed), create a pull request in the docs repo and request at least one reviewer from an adjacent team.

4) Retirement
- If a runbook is unused for 12+ months and tests fail, flag for retirement. Keep an archive list with rationale and last-tested date.

Runbook content standard (template)

- Title: short descriptive name
- Summary: one-sentence purpose
- Service(s) affected: list
- Severity mapping: P1/P2/P3 descriptions for this runbook
- Preconditions: required credentials, network access, tooling (kubectl, pdctl, ssh)
- Initial detection: alert names and metrics that trigger use (SLO threshold names)
- Immediate containment steps (ordered, numbered)
- Diagnostics (commands and expected outputs)
- Escalation matrix: who to call at 0/15/30/60 minutes
- Rollforward/rollback instructions (if applicable)
- Post-incident checklist: evidence to collect, owners for RCA actions, timeline capture notes
- Test plan: how to safely exercise this runbook in game days

Example diagnostics snippets

- Check runtime pod health:
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
- Inspect logs for OOMKill or liveness probes:
  kubectl -n redwood logs [pod] --since=10m | grep -E "OOMKilled|liveness probe failed"
- Check queue depth (Redis):
  redis-cli -h redis-svc info | grep "instantaneous_ops_per_sec"

Incident ownership ladder

- T0 (First 10 minutes): Pager recipient acknowledges and triages. If obvious containment step exists, operator executes it.
- T10 (10–30 minutes): Incident Commander (IC) appointed by on-call rotation. IC declares impact and channels (bridge + Slack channel) and assigns roles: comms, triage lead, and mitigation lead.
- T30 (30–90 minutes): Service owner / engineering lead joins. IC maintains timeline and coordinates cross-team dependencies.
- T90+: If unresolved, escalate to SRE manager and Platform Eng lead; consider customer notifications and credits policy.

SLO & severity mapping examples (illustrative)

- P99 latency SLO: <= 150 ms for request-path /v1/generate (global).
- Error rate SLO: 0.02 (2%) errors per 1m window.
- Severity mapping:
  - Sev1 / P1: Revenue-impacting, >50% customers affected, SLO broken for >10 minutes.
  - Sev2 / P2: Significant degradation for subset of customers, SLO degraded but not fully broken.
  - Sev3 / P3: Minor customer impact, isolated errors or performance blips.

On-call rotation stewardship

- Rotation length: 1 week. Primary on-call with a secondary backup.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in PagerDuty notes & Slack):
  1) Current ongoing incidents and bridge links
  2) Outstanding action items requiring follow-up
  3) Recent runbook changes or flaky alerts
  4) Contactable escalations and out-of-hours numbers
- Fairness rules: no more than 2 weekend rotations per quarter; swaps must be logged and approved by the manager.
- Shadowing: new on-call engineers must shadow 2 rotations and complete the on-call checklist exercise in a game day within first 30 days.

Game day (exercise) playbook

Purpose: validate runbooks, surface gaps in escalations, exercise comms and status page flows.

Planning timeline:
- T-21 days: propose scenario and get approval from relevant service owner and SRE lead.
- T-7 days: announce to org with scope and blackout windows.
- T-0: execute exercise in staging or canary region.
- T+1 day: publish game day findings and action items.

Sample game day scenario (KV cache eviction storm):
- Objective: ensure runbook steps contain safe containment for high-throughput prefix-cache misses.
- Roles: IC (SRE on call), operator (service on call), comms (product liaison), observer (engineering steward).
- Exercises:
  1) Trigger synthetic traffic to simulate cache thundering (lower QPS to safe window first).
  2) Follow runbook: rollback deploy, throttle traffic, enable fallback model variant.
  3) Evaluate status page message dissemination and internal bridging.

Postmortem and RCA standard

- When to write: all P1 incidents and either a P2 with customer impact or any incident that required multi-team coordination.
- Template (must be filled):
  - Title: incident-service-date-impact
  - Summary: 2–4 sentence summary
  - Impact: timeline of customer-facing symptoms, number of affected customers, duration
  - Root cause analysis: facts, timeline, gap analysis (tools, people, process)
  - Remediation actions: owner, ETA, verification steps
  - Preventative actions: what will change in monitoring, runbook, or code
  - Postmortem severity and lessons learned
  - Signal evidence: links to logs, graph snapshots, and saved traces
- Postmortem review: present to incident review board within 5 business days. Action items must have owners & due dates.

Status page and customer comms templates

- Principles: be timely, concise, factual, and avoid speculation. Provide regular cadence updates (every 30–60 minutes for P1 until mitigation).

Template: Major Outage (P1)
- Title: [Major Outage] Service name — Degraded / Unavailable
- Initial post (15 min): We are investigating reports of degraded performance for the /v1/generate endpoint. Impact: some customers may see increased latency or errors. We are actively investigating and have started mitigation actions. Next update: in 30 minutes.
- Follow-up post (30 min): Root cause update or actions taken (e.g., "We identified a KV cache thundering event caused by recent rollout X; rolling back to previous model variant and throttling upstream traffic.")
- Restore post: Confirm restoration, provide ETA for full verification, and link to postmortem when available.

Template: Degraded Performance (P2)
- Title: [Degraded Performance] Service name — Elevated error rate
- Initial post: We are seeing an elevated error rate on request-path X affecting a subset of customers. Engineers are investigating. If you are experiencing issues, please contact support with request ID. Next update: 60 minutes.

Customer-facing email snippet (for enterprise customers)

Subject: Incident update — [Service] — {Short description}
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We are writing to update you about an incident affecting {Service}. Impact: {brief impact summary}. Our engineers are actively mitigating the issue and we anticipate a resolution within {ETA}. We will provide another update at {time}.

If you have urgent concerns, reply to this email or contact your account team.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support (on-call team)

Operational metrics & evidence collection

- Minimum evidence to collect during incident: start/end time, commands run and outputs, screenshots of monitoring graphs, key log snippets, and affected customer IDs. Save snapshots to incident bundle in S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/{incident-id}/.
- Retention: incident bundles retained for 24 months. Postmortems and runbook changes must reference bundle paths.

Runbook testing and acceptance criteria

- Acceptance test: each runbook must have at least one automated smoke test (synthetic check) run monthly. Tests should validate that diagnostics produce expected outputs and that containment steps are safe in staging.
- Test results should be attached to runbook metadata with last-test date and test-run author.

Escalation and credits policy (brief)

- If an incident leads to an SLA breach (as defined by our contracts), the SRE manager will coordinate with finance and legal on credits. Escalation to account team occurs within 60 minutes for enterprise customers.

Appendix: quick-check triage checklist

1) Acknowledge page and create incident channel.
2) Determine scope: internal-only, subset of customers, or platform-wide.
3) Check SLO dashboards for P99 and error rate.
4) Run core diagnostics (see runbook).
5) If containment exists, execute and mark time.
6) Publish status page initial message and email/Slack to account team.

Appendix: contact matrix (example)

- PagerDuty escalation: On-call primary -> backup -> SRE manager -> Eng Director
- Slack: #inc-ops (bridge), @oncall-team (escalation mentions)

Appendix: sample runbook header (copy into top of each runbook)

Title: runtime-prefix-eviction-P1
Service: redwood-runtime
Steward: Aisha Patel (or assigned engineer)
Created: 2024-11-12
Last reviewed: 2025-02-12
Changelog:
- 2025-02-12: clarified eviction thresholds and added redis diagnostics

Feedback and continued improvement

- If you identify gaps in this policy or the runbook template, open a docs PR and tag @Runbook-Curation. We will incorporate changes monthly and publish a changelog.

Related resources

- SLO dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/slo
- Incident bundle S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/
- Runbook repo: https://git.internal.redwood/runbooks

Approved by: SRE Lead (Diego Morales), Platform Eng Lead (Priya Singh)
